key_insight: Raising the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio made Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings denser and better bonded, with the best overall surface quality and adhesion at 1.2.
engineering_relevance: Process-gas control is an effective lever for tuning coating quality in flame-sprayed wear- and corrosion-resistant layers on AISI 321 steel.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied the O2/C2H2 ratio to 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 while monitoring spray conditions with Accuraspray 4.0.
Characterized porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports porosity dropping from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, adhesion rising from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa, and peak microhardness of 1051.7 HV at O2/C2H2 = 1.1.
watch_item: The optimal gas ratio may be system- and substrate-specific, so these results should be validated for other spray setups, part geometries, and service conditions.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
